ImageDescription.value:
Jain Statue called Paluppar, Jayamkondacholapuram:
Jayamkondacholapuram is located about a hundred kilometres northeast of Trichy, on the way to Virudhachalam. The stone image is erected on the bund of a water tank, placed over a stone pedestal. Locally referred to as 'Paluppar', the image represents Lord Buddha in a meditative posture. He is shown wearing a transparent robe draped across the shoulder. The facial features include a short forehead with an auspicious circular dot, half-closed eyes with raised eyebrows in a contemplative mood, a sharp nose, and elongated ears. The hair is depicted as tight curled coils, culminating in a tuft above. The branches of a fig tree, forming an umbrella shape, rise above the arched halo. Stylistically, the image is datable to around the 11th century CE.
